findings.location: Set B 새 예 ‘진행자가 사진을 가리켰다’ → model ‘첫 사진’ / EN ‘first photo’
findings.problem: The Korean fresh data gives a photo but no ordinal; the model and translations add that it is the first photo. It does not affect the immediate-sequence answer, but source-preserving modelling would avoid this small addition.
findings.proposal: Remove ‘첫’ from the KO model and ‘first’/‘erste’ from the corresponding EN/DE fresh-case text, keeping the event ‘불이 켜지기가 바쁘게 진행자가 사진을 가리켰다.’

findings.location: Opening EN ‘Joy turns Dokkaebi’s “perhaps” into “certainly.” He says, …’
findings.problem: ‘He’ most naturally refers to the preceding subject Joy, but KO explicitly assigns the quoted line to Dokkaebi. This risks switching the speaker and also invites an unsupported gender reading for Joy.
findings.proposal: Replace ‘He says,’ with ‘Dokkaebi says,’. Keep the quoted translation otherwise unchanged.

findings.location: Fresh-production row -게 마련이다 EN model ‘Questions are natural at first, so time should be set aside; none are recorded yet.’
findings.problem: KO reports the facilitator's general expectation and advice (‘…라며 시간을 두자고 했다’). EN turns it into the narrator's unqualified principle and omits who proposed time for questions. This weakens the row's explicit source/expectation distinction.
findings.proposal: Replace EN model with: ‘The facilitator said that questions naturally arise with a new task and suggested setting aside time for them. No actual questions have been asked yet.’ Align DE to retain the facilitator's reported advice as well.

findings.location: Modern script last EN row ‘Beside the ground-level desk marked 1층. Ask there which device is working.’
findings.problem: KO locates the information desk on the ground floor, labelled 1층 in Korean; EN makes the desk itself marked 1층. ‘Which device is working’ also presupposes a working device, while KO asks whether the intended device works. This is the reader-facing location/check instruction.
findings.proposal: Replace EN row with: ‘Beside the information desk on the ground floor (1층). Ask at the desk whether the device you want to use is working.’ Align DE's floor label and conditional function check.

findings.location: 생활 전이 extended EN proposal example ‘Let's get a photo guide ready … have it checked tomorrow. We can reconsider the video afterwards.’
findings.problem: The KO model explicitly conditions distribution on tomorrow's accuracy check (‘내일 정확성 확인 뒤 배포’). The English example retains a planned check but drops the distribution-after-check relationship. Preserving implementation conditions is the stated mediation goal.
findings.proposal: Replace EN three-sentence proposal with: ‘Let’s prioritise a photo guide for the workshop in two days. Seven of eighteen participants asked about the tool names. We can distribute it after an accuracy check tomorrow and consider the video later.’ Keep the participant instruction; align DE to the same check-before-distribution condition.
